as_told.title: Tim Taylor's downloads from non-human intelligences

tellings.quote: One of the most curious aspects of Taylor's story is his claim that he receives downloads from an intelligence he believes is non-human.

tellings.quote: Tyler has an unusual ability to predict the future, which explains in part his improbable success. He credits his ‘protocol’ with allowing him to predict outcomes, and maybe this is true, I don’t know. His protocol involves physical and mental exercises.

plain: The story is that a successful American businessman named Timothy Taylor says his ideas came to him as "downloads" from a non-human intelligence. Michels tells it several times, drawing on American Cosmic, a book by the religion scholar Diana Pasulka, who knew Taylor. Michels says Taylor claims much of his work came from these downloads, and that he believes they come from an intelligence that is not human. He adds that Taylor says the downloads were made possible by "protocols" he followed. If true, it would mean some real-world inventions and businesses came from contact with something non-human. Pasulka's own words appear in an interview about her book, published on 21 December 2018, where Taylor goes by the name Tyler. She says Tyler "has an unusual ability to predict the future, which explains in part his improbable success." She says he credits his protocol, which "involves physical and mental exercises", with letting him predict outcomes, adding "maybe this is true, I don't know." So she keeps her own doubt beside his claim. The step from a protocol that predicts outcomes to business ideas downloaded from a non-human source is the tellers' reading of her book, which this interview neither states nor rules out.

discussion.by: INTERVIEW: D.W Pasulka brings 'American Cosmic' to the UFO forefront
discussion.text: Here Pasulka writes that Tyler "credits his ‘protocol’ with allowing him to predict outcomes, and maybe this is true, I don’t know", a protocol of "physical and mental exercises"; she keeps her own doubt beside his claim. The step from a protocol that predicts outcomes to business ideas downloaded from a non-human intelligence is the tellers' reading of the book, which this interview neither states nor excludes.
